title: GPU pool saturation: congestion control playbook, telemetry hardening, and targeted mitigations
creator: Ava Chen
description: Follow-up work for a hosted API GPU capacity event where slow scale-up + admission gating produced multi-minute queue buildups and elevated tail latency for customer requests. This ticket captures the timeline, root cause analysis, short-term mitigations already deployed, and the medium-term hardening tasks with clear owners and estimates.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-09 a sustained traffic spike against the hosted text-generation endpoint triggered slow autoscaler response and conservative admission controls. Pending queue depth grew in multiple GPU pools, causing increased throttling, elevated request latency, and customer-facing 429/504 surface at peaks. Impact lasted ~48 minutes for the worst-affected pools and degraded throughput for ~2 hours as capacity recovered.
timeline: 2026-03-09T09:18Z - Traffic surge begins; atypical long-context batch requests from a single tenant observed (X tokens/request increase ~3x).
2026-03-09T09:24Z - Pool pending count crossed soft-threshold; admission controller began rejecting lower-priority requests. Metrics: pending_count rose from 8 to 420 in 6 minutes.
2026-03-09T09:30Z - Autoscaler evaluated scale signal but selected conservative scale-up path (single-step allocation) due to cooldown config; additional GPU allocation delayed by 90s.
2026-03-09T09:31Z - First customer complaints (high latency, partial failures) reported to SRE via PagerDuty.
2026-03-09T09:36Z - Manual intervention: SRE triggered emergency scale-up to burst pool and relaxed admission score thresholds for priority customers.
2026-03-09T09:58Z - Queue depth returned to normal for primary pools; degraded throughput continued as KV cache warms and spawned worker processes ramp up.
2026-03-09T11:15Z - Incident declared resolved for SLA tracking; follow-up investigation started.
2026-03-10T14:00Z - Telemetry gap found: pending request duration metric missing for several old pool shapes; alerting did not fire as expected.
2026-03-11T10:20Z - Short-term mitigations deployed: reduced autoscaler cooldown, temporary admission relaxation, and priming job for KV caches for affected customers.
root_cause: A constellation of issues created a race where demand outpaced the fast-path autoscaling and mitigation controls: (1) autoscaler cooldown and single-step allocation policy prevented rapid burst provisioning; (2) admission controller scoring used a static threshold tuned for steady-state traffic, which caused over-rejection during gradual buildup; (3) KV cache cold starts and model worker spin-up latency extended effective recovery time; (4) observability gaps (no pending_duration SLO and missing per-shape queue metrics) delayed automated detection and response.
mitigations_implemented: Reduced autoscaler cooldown from 90s to 15s for burst class pools (temporary change) - deployed 2026-03-11
Introduced an emergency 'burst' allocation path to allow 2x allocation in a single step when pending_count growth rate > 100/s - gated by rate limits - deployed 2026-03-11
Relaxed admission-score floor for priority-tier customers to avoid wholesale rejection during transient ramps - deployed 2026-03-11
Added a customer-targeted cache-priming job (best-effort) to warm KV caches for sustained long-context flows - rolled out to 3 tenants as canary on 2026-03-11
metrics_observed: Median request latency increased from 120ms to 1.1s during peak
Token throughput dropped by 37% across affected pools during saturation window
Autoscaler allocation lag: median 75s between scale signal and usable GPU availability for default path
